$comment: Named RECORDING PRESETS — one per physical place Heath shoots from.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A preset is a measured, human-verified answer to
'given this room, this camera distance and this furniture, what part of
the sensor is the actual picture?'. That answer does not change between
takes as long as he stands in the same spot, so it belongs in config
with its derivation recorded — not as a constant inside a function where
nobody can see what it was measured against or when it stops being true.
A preset is a BASELINE FOR THE FACE TRACKER, NOT A RIGID CROP.
face-track-crop.js uses baselineCrop to answer two questions — how tight
is the shot (zoom) and where does the subject sit inside it (faceAnchor.
withinCrop) — and then MOVES that window to follow the face. A preset
applied as a static crop will amputate him: he drifts laterally during a
take and a raised hand leaves the baseline rect entirely in the last
seconds of the 2026-09-22 source.
ROTATION CAVEAT. All coordinates are in DISPLAY space — the frame AFTER
the container's rotation metadata has been applied. Phone footage is
commonly stored 3840x2160 landscape with a -90 display matrix and
presents as 2160x3840 portrait. ffmpeg/ffprobe apply that matrix by
default on decode, so these numbers match what you get from a plain
`ffmpeg -i src -frames:v 1 out.png`. They do NOT match the raw stored
width/height reported by `ffprobe -show_streams`. Always compare against
displayWidth/displayHeight, never stream width/height.
RESOLUTION INDEPENDENCE. baselineCrop is absolute pixels for the source
it was derived against; baselineCropNormalized is the same rect as
fractions of the display frame. The engine works at an intermediate
resolution (edit.js caps the long edge at 2880, so 2160x3840 becomes
1620x2880), so ONLY the normalized form is ever applied. The absolute
pixels are kept so the derivation stays auditable.

kitchen-island.label: Kitchen island — standing behind the counter, phone on the far side
description: Heath shoots from across a kitchen island he cannot move, so the
camera sits further back than a normal talking-head distance. Raw
frame: he is small in frame, the counter/placemat/cutting board eat
the bottom third, and there is far too much headroom (ceiling and
light fixture). This preset punches in 1.61x to recover a normal
shot: counter gone, eyes on the upper third, hands still in frame

method: Crop rect chosen by eye against the raw frame, then verified on a
13-frame contact sheet sampled every ~2 s across the full 27.3 s
take and looked at directly — not inferred from face-box math.
Face positions across the same 13 frames were then measured with
the engine's own RFB-320 detector to record faceAnchor.

kitchen-island.$baselineZoomComment: displayHeight / baselineCrop.h = 3840 / 2386. This is the WIDE shot — the verified framing — not a maximum.

$comment: Where the face sat when the crop was derived, measured with the
engine's own detector across 11 non-transient frames (t=2..22 s;
t=0 and t=26 excluded as lean-in outliers). withinCrop is the
tracking target: face-track-crop.js keeps the face at this
position inside the crop window, which reproduces the verified
baseline exactly when he is at his home position and follows him
when he is not.
A preset is a home framing, not a lock. gainX/gainY scale how much
of the face's excursion from its home position the crop follows.
gainX is high because lateral drift is real movement — he shifts
left around the middle of the take. gainY is lower because most
vertical face motion is head bob, and a frame that bobs with his
head reads as a handheld wobble. maxExcursionFrac caps how far the
window may travel from home as a fraction of the crop size, so one
bad detection cannot fling the frame across the room.
What shot-plan.js should derive its wide/punch range from. wide IS
the verified baseline; punch is tighter. Absolute values, already
relative to baselineZoom — they are NOT the engine's generic
defaults, which top out at punchZoomMax 1.6 and would clamp this
preset's own baseline of 1.6095 back down, silently undoing it.
Signature of 'shot from across the island': a portrait 9:16 frame
in which the face is SMALL (he is far away) and HIGH (the counter
occupies the bottom). Both bounds are wide relative to the
measured spread and are still cleanly disjoint from the previous
arm's-length source (22054.mp4, the trial_06/07 take), which
measures faceHeightFrac 0.342-0.433 and faceCyFrac 0.503-0.581.
Margin on faceHeightFrac is 0.24 vs 0.342; on faceCyFrac 0.45 vs
0.503. Detection is a match on BOTH, on a majority of sampled
frames, or it does not fire.

notes: BASELINE, NOT A RIGID CROP — see the top-level $comment. Applied
statically this rect clips his raised hand in the final seconds.
The island cannot be moved, so the camera distance is fixed; if he
ever shoots from a different side of it, re-derive rather than nudge.
Audio from this setup is a single DJI lav into ONE input — expect a
Re-derive if: he changes where he stands, the phone moves, or the
camera's focal length / crop factor changes (different phone, or
the same phone on a different lens).
